title: An Explicit Percent Type
prompt_md:
## Goal Build a small wrapper type around an integer percentage, using an `explicit` converting constructor so a bare integer is never silently treated as a `Percent`. ## The feature (lesson 14.16) Give `Percent` an `explicit` single-argument constructor taking the percentage as an `int`, a `value()` accessor, and an `of(int total)` member that returns `value * total / 100` (integer arithmetic). Marking the constructor `explicit` means callers must write `Percent{p}` rather than relying on an implicit `int`-to-`Percent` conversion. ## Input - Line 1: integer `N` (1 ≤ N ≤ 10) - Next `N` lines: two integers per line — the percentage `p` and a `total` ## Output For each line, print `

% of = ` where `result` is `p * total / 100` using integer division.

title: Disambiguate With explicit
prompt_md:
## Goal
Use `explicit` to control overload resolution: a function is overloaded for two wrapper types that are both built from an `int`, and you must make a call with a bare `int` resolve to a specific one.

## The feature (lesson 14.16)
`Celsius` and `Fahrenheit` each store one `int` and each have a single-argument `int` constructor. The provided `report` is overloaded for both. The call `report(x)` in `main` passes a plain `int`. If BOTH constructors allow implicit conversion the call is ambiguous and will not compile; if exactly one is left as an implicit converting constructor, that overload is chosen. Mark the right constructor `explicit` so `report(x)` unambiguously selects the `Celsius` overload.

## Input
- Line 1: integer `N` (1 ≤ N ≤ 10)
- Next `N` lines: one integer per line

## Output
For each value, print `Celsius <value>` — produced because the `int` implicitly converts to `Celsius` while the `Fahrenheit` constructor is `explicit`.
